story: prerequisites → run → validation → maker approval → finance approval → lock → payslips → bank file → reconciliation

steps.action: Read the payroll prerequisites for the tenant before opening a run
steps.expected: The payroll dashboard states how many ACTIVE employees were checked against salary assignments, payroll profiles, IBANs and statutory readiness, and names every remaining gap.
steps.observed: The prerequisites panel reports 14 active employees checked.

steps.action: REFUSAL — try to activate a KSA expat who has no GOSI reference and no Iqama number
steps.expected: The activation is refused with a structured 422 naming the missing statutory data, and the employee stays Draft. An employee who cannot lawfully be paid must never join a payroll population.
steps.observed: Draft employee #44 (SA, Indian national) created; activation refused with HTTP 422 employee_not_activatable. Activate-blocking: IqamaNumber. Pay-blocking: GosiReference, IqamaExpiry.

persisted.via: fresh GET of the employee — a refused activation must leave it Draft

capture.reason: Deliberately so: this refusal was driven through the API, so there is no screen of it to photograph; the 422 body recorded below is the whole of the evidence. A picture of the employee list here would show a screen that has nothing to do with the refusal, which is exactly the substitution this harness exists to prevent. The UI path for the same refusal is listed under Not run.

steps.action: Create the payroll run for the first period that does not have one
steps.expected: A new run exists in Draft for that period, and the list renders every run the API returned.
steps.observed: Run for Sep 2026 created in Draft as a9e97248-45d6-41c4-ad47-2db6759327fa.

steps.action: Process the run so every employee on it gets a calculated salary slip
steps.expected: The run leaves Draft for Processed and carries a non-zero employee count and net-pay total.

steps.action: Run payroll validation on the processed run and read every finding
steps.expected: Validation completes with ZERO errors, and every warning it does return is one this story can explain by code — an unexplained warning fails the step rather than being counted and carried into approval.
steps.observed: Validation returned 29 finding(s): 0 error(s), 29 warning(s); codes: GOSI_COHORT_NOT_RECORDED, WARN_ARREARS_LOOKBACK_TRUNCATED, WARN_GOSI_RATES_REQUIRE_SIGNOFF.

persisted.via: fresh GET of the saved validation results

warningsExplained.GOSI_COHORT_NOT_RECORDED: 14× — The employee has no GOSI first-registration date, so the engine cannot tell which contribution schedule applies and computes on the pre-3-July-2024 one. It is a WARNING and not an error by design: the pre-2024 schedule is the correct answer for everyone hired before that date, and the date is recorded on the employee's Payroll tab once known. The fixture employees are provisioned without it, so this fires once per employee and is expected here. The related GOSI_NEW_ENTRANT_SCHEDULE_NOT_MODELLED code is an ERROR and would block approval; it does not appear on this run, and the step asserts zero errors.

steps.action: The HR Manager (maker) approves the run and sends it to Finance
steps.expected: The run moves to Pending Finance Review, and the approval chain records the maker step. The maker is told, on screen, that their approval is not the final one.
steps.observed: Screen and API agree: 14 employees, gross SAR 138,250.00, net SAR 119,730.47. The run is now Pending Finance Review.

steps.action: REFUSAL — the maker tries to approve a second time and complete the run alone
steps.expected: No approval control survives on the run the maker already signed, the API refuses a second approval with HTTP 400, and — the part that matters — the run does not move.
steps.observed: Three approval controls absent from the maker's card; the API answered HTTP 400: {"message":"You cannot approve this run at its current stage."}

api.detail: {"message":"You cannot approve this run at its current stage."}

steps.action: The Finance Approver — a different authorised person — gives the final approval
steps.expected: The run reaches Approved, reads as ready to lock, and the approval chain holds BOTH the maker step and the finance step, signed by two different people.
steps.observed: Approval chain: FinanceReview → PayrollReview, signed by 2 distinct users.

screenAssertion.pattern: Payroll run has been approved and is ready to lock.

steps.action: REFUSAL — open the bank export while the run is Approved but not yet Locked
steps.expected: Create Payment Batch is disabled, and the screen says why, naming the run's actual current status rather than a generic message. No batch exists.
steps.observed: Create Payment Batch is disabled and the screen states "This run is Approved." — the lock, not the approval, is the gate.

screenAssertion.pattern: /A payment batch can only be created once the run is/

persisted.via: fresh GET of the run's payment batches — none may exist yet

steps.action: The Finance Approver locks the approved run
steps.expected: The run reaches Locked, carries a lock timestamp, and offers no further lifecycle control.
steps.observed: The run is Locked and exposes no Lock or Process control.

steps.action: Generate the payslips for the locked run
steps.expected: Exactly 14 payslips, one per distinct employee, each with a real payslip number, and each published to employee self-service (the run is locked, so the month is already being paid).

steps.action: Create the payment batch now that the run is locked
steps.expected: The control is enabled, the blocking notice is gone, and the batch's total equals the run's net pay with one payment line per employee.
steps.observed: Batch PAY-202609-170039 created in Draft for SAR 119,730.47.

steps.action: Generate the WPS/SIF bank file (generation only — this must not pay anybody)
steps.expected: The batch reaches File Generated with a named file, a content hash, one record per employee and a total equal to the run's net pay. The run stays Locked, the batch is not settled, and no payment record says paid.

persisted.via: fresh GET of the run, the batch and every payment record — the "nobody was paid" check

steps.action: Reconcile the displayed totals against the source records
steps.expected: The reconciliation report's current-period gross and net equal the run's own totals, which equal the sum of the per-employee salary slips, which equal the sum of the payment lines, which equal the wage file total.
steps.observed: Reconciliation: headcount 14, gross 138250.00, net 119730.47, 0 flagged variance(s).

persisted.via: fresh GETs of the run, its salary slips, the bank payment lines and the reconciliation report

defects.title: The KSA statutory activation floor is bypassed for any employee created without a country
defects.detail: POST /api/employees sets Employee.CountryCode ONLY from the first complianceRecords entry (EmployeeManagementService.CreateAsync) and never falls back to the country of the company the employee is attached to. GccReadinessFloor.Resolve("") returns an empty requirement list, so EnsureActivatable finds nothing to enforce and a non-GCC expat with no Iqama number and no GOSI reference is activated into a Saudi legal entity with HTTP 200. GET /api/employees/field-catalog states the intended rule — "Explicit countryCode wins, else the company's country" — so the derivation is specified and simply absent on this path. An employee activated this way occupies an active seat and is a candidate for a payroll population while being unpayable under KSA rules.
evidence: Step R1 (refusal-incomplete-employee): identical employee WITH a compliance record naming SA → HTTP 422 employee_not_activatable, blocking IqamaNumber, pay-blocking GosiReference.
Step R1b (this tripwire): identical employee WITHOUT it → countryCode "", HTTP 200, Active.
Zayra.Api.Tests/EmployeeActivationGateTests.cs sets CountryCode = "SA" directly on its fixture entities, so it covers the gate but never the derivation — the blind spot.
defects.resolvedNote: Fixed after this run. The observation above is left exactly as recorded on build 64bab568c9ce72665c605ef39da7467d15ac2d82 and has not been rewritten.

defects.title: A background AI-insights fetch 403s on every payroll screen and raises a user-facing "Access Denied" error toast
defects.detail: GET /api/ai/insights is issued automatically by the payroll module on mount. For any persona without the AI insight permission — here the HR Manager and the Finance Approver, both of whom are doing exactly their job — it returns 403, and the frontend renders it as "Access Denied — You do not have permission to perform this action. Please contact your administrator." The payroll transaction underneath succeeded every time. The effect is that a correct, completed payroll action is presented to the operator as a permission failure. A background panel the user did not ask for should degrade silently (hide the panel), not raise a blocking error.
evidence: 5 such 403s across steps: prerequisites, validation, finance-approval, payslips, reconciliation
Visible in img/11-payslips.jpg — the toast sits over a screen that correctly shows 14 payslips, all published to ESS.
Affects the HR Manager and Finance Approver personas; the Admin persona holds the permission and sees no toast.

defectsResolvedNote: Both defects below were FIXED in PR #162 (the KSA activation floor is bypassed for an employee created without a country; the background AI-insights 403 raising an "Access Denied" toast). This bundle is the unaltered record of the run it describes, made on build 64bab568c9ce72665c605ef39da7467d15ac2d82, which predates that fix — the images, the step table and the observations below have deliberately NOT been re-recorded or edited, because a record that is rewritten after the fact stops being evidence. Read them as what was true on that build. The spec has since changed: the R1b tripwire step is gone and its case is folded into R1, which now makes both create calls and asserts the same 422 for each, so a fresh run records 14 steps and neither defect.
